headline: DepEd Says 9,142 Schools Shifted to Distance Learning Amid Neneng, Habagat
seoTitle: 9,142 Schools Shift to Distance Learning | FMB News
seoDescription: The approved FMB News midday brief reports that 9,142 schools across 18 Luzon jurisdictions shifted away from in-person classes amid Neneng and Habagat weather risks.
deck: The scale of the shift shows how prolonged severe weather is disrupting classroom instruction across Luzon.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The approved FMB News midday package reports that 9,142 public and private schools across Metro Manila and 17 Luzon provinces suspended in-person classes and activated Alternative Delivery Modes on August 19.
The package cites DepEd disaster monitoring and says the shift coincided with continuing rainfall warnings linked to Tropical Depression Neneng and the Southwest Monsoon.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Alternative Delivery Modes can include printed modules and asynchronous or remote learning, depending on school capacity and local instructions.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Large-scale learning disruption can compound existing education gaps, making both safety and continuity planning important during extended weather emergencies.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch DepEd for updated school counts, return-to-class guidance, damage assessments and support for affected learners and teachers.

sources.title: Official DepEd advisories and disaster monitoring
